pr_body:
This PR completes the implementation of resource destruction only using the resource's state (configuration is still required for providers).  By making sure destroy provisioners cannot reference other resources (more info in #23559), there is no need to connect resources to other values during destroy, preventing numerous cycle issues. 

This also completes the implementation of storing the destroy references in the state (more info in #23252). The `NodeAbstractResourceInstance.References` implementation can now be simplified because there will be no more `depends_on` references from the state during destroy. This also means we no longer need to search again for destroy dependencies during apply, since we stored them already, removing an extra graph-building and traversal step.

Finally we greatly simplify the `CBDEdgeTransformer`, because we now know that the resource destroy nodes can only depend on other resource destroy nodes and can easily reverse the required `GraphNodeCreator` edges. 

Closes #14548
Closes #16237
Closes #17944
Closes #18026
Closes #18088

issue_context.title: Propagation of create_before_destroy = true
issue_context.body:
### Terraform Version
```
Terraform v0.12.0
+ provider.random v2.1.2
+ provider.tls v2.0.1
```

### Terraform Configuration Files
```hcl
resource "random_integer" "bits" {
  min = 2048
  max = 4096
}
resource "tls_private_key" "terraform" {
  algorithm = "RSA"
  rsa_bits = random_integer.bits.result
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

```

### Expected Behavior
Only the `tls_private_key` should be created before destroy.

### Actual Behavior
Both resources will create the replacement first then destroy the old instance.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. `terraform init`
2. `terraform apply`
3. `terraform taint random_integer.bits`
4. `terraform taint tls_private_key.terraform`
5. `terraform plan`

### Additional Context
Output from terraform plan (simplified):
```
An execution plan has been generated and is shown below.
Resource actions are indicated with the following symbols:
+/- create replacement and then destroy

Terraform will perform the following actions:

  # random_integer.bits is tainted, so must be replaced
+/- resource "random_integer" "bits" {
      ~ id     = "3232" -> (known after apply)
        max    = 4096
        min    = 2048
      ~ result = 3232 -> (known after apply)
    }

  # tls_private_key.terraform is tainted, so must be replaced
+/- resource "tls_private_key" "terraform" {
        algorithm                  = "RSA"
        ecdsa_curve                = "P224"
      ~ id                         = "3ff51c9479f37e8906fd4bda0c07cce5bccbc57a" -> (known after apply)
      ~ private_key_pem            = "<ommited for simplicity>" -> (known after apply)
      ~ public_key_fingerprint_md5 = "85:40:0e:0c:06:c1:dd:c5:58:e2:2a:14:00:67:d7:1b" -> (known after apply)
      ~ public_key_openssh         = "<ommited for simplicity>" -> (known after apply)
      ~ public_key_pem             = "<ommited for simplicity>" -> (known after apply)
      ~ rsa_bits                   = 3232 -> (known after apply)
    }

Plan: 2 to add, 0 to change, 2 to destroy.

```
Setting a lifecycle with `create_before_destroy = false` for `random_integer` has no effect.

Seems like the `create_before_destroy = true` is being propagated via the graph. I don't know if it is a bug or an undocumented feature (I hope its a bug). Even if it is a feature "overriding" the `create_before_destroy` on `random_integer` should work.

The terraform configuration given is just an example chosen for its simplicity. The problem will also arise with other resources.
comments:
Hi @Lasering,

What you're seeing here is the expected behavior. Because the `tls_private_key` depends on `random_integer`, the `random_integer` can't be destroyed until after the `tls_private_key`. The new `tls_private_key` depends on the new `random_integer`, so that has to be made first, hence forcing the `random_integer` to be `create_before_destroy` as well. 

You can't override `create_before_destroy` on `random_integer`, because the ordering of resource requires it, and there would otherwise be dependency cycles in the graph.

That makes sense. I guess then the docs should explain it, or at least mention it (at least I couldn't find any explanation).

I don't understand why overriding the `create_before_destroy` would cause cycles. What I can see as a "problem" is using the "old" value instead of the "new" value.

There may some place that this makes sense to add. These details generally aren't documented other than that Terraform will order the resource dependencies as necessary.

Examples of this get convoluted easily, but simplest way I've found to state the problem is: in any non-trivial acyclic subgraph, reversing half the edges is likely to result in a cycle ("overriding" `create_before_destroy` on a subset of the graph amounts to reversing the dependencies).

The documentation could mention it here: https://www.terraform.io/docs/configuration/resources.html#create_before_destroy

Checking if a graph/subgraph has loops isn't that expensive computationally. The plan/apply could check and if there were loops it could complain, or if an overridden create_before_destroy was present hint that it could be the cause.

Yes, the docs at one point had something like that (back when users had to manually add `create_before_destroy`). Declaring that all dependencies have to be able to handle this parameter should suffice.
